availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

Trigger: write a readme, improve the readme, README structure, quick start section, getting started guide, project introduction, onboarding documentation, README template.

availableCommands.name: recall
availableCommands.description: Cross-session memory recall. Use when asked about past decisions, prior work, what was discussed previously, or to continue from where a session left off. Use to persist decisions and lessons learned. Trigger: "what did we decide", "last session", "previously", "recall", "remind me", "continue from where we left off", "what was the decision".

availableCommands.name: release-protocol
availableCommands.description: Cut tagged releases safely with SemVer, changelog roll, and validation gates. Use when releasing, bumping version, tagging, shipping, or deciding what version to use. Trigger: release, tag, version bump, ship, publish, cut a release, what version.

availableCommands.name: research-methodology
availableCommands.description: Structured research process for investigating topics and producing findings. Use when exploring unfamiliar domains, evaluating options, or gathering evidence to inform decisions.

availableCommands.name: research-output
availableCommands.description: Structured output format for research findings. Use when producing research results, investigation reports, or any findings that should be reusable across sessions. Ensures sources, related topics, and tools are always captured alongside the findings.

availableCommands.name: review-new-work
availableCommands.description: Incremental and full-history repository review with resumable adoption batches. Use when reviewing new work, initializing review tracking, reviewing all work to date, resuming historical review, inspecting unreviewed commits, or reviewing changed tickets. Trigger: review new work, adopt repository, review all history, resume review, review marker, unreviewed commits.

availableCommands.name: script-authoring
availableCommands.description: Best practices for writing tool and helper scripts. Use when creating bash scripts, automation tools, CLI utilities, or any executable that will be run repeatedly by humans or agents.

availableCommands.name: skill-authoring
availableCommands.description: Write and improve agent-loadable skills. Use when creating a new skill, improving an existing skill's activation, restructuring a skill that's too broad, writing skill frontmatter, or diagnosing why a skill doesn't trigger. Trigger: new skill, write a skill, skill format, skill template, activation trigger, skill description, SKILL.md.

availableCommands.name: spec-driven-development
availableCommands.description: Plan projects using PLAN.md and per-feature spec files. Use when starting a new project, breaking a project into phases, writing specs for features, or when someone says 'let's plan this out' or 'write a spec'. Trigger: PLAN.md, spec, feature spec, project plan, phases, task graph, validation criteria.

availableCommands.name: study-all-references
availableCommands.description: Batch study all repos/tools in .references/. Dispatches parallel subagents to document each, then distills learnings into steering/skills. Use when onboarding to a project with multiple reference repos.

availableCommands.name: study-reference
availableCommands.description: Deep-dive a tool or repo in .references/. Documents purpose, usage, novel patterns, and distills learnings into steering/skills. Use when onboarding a new reference repo or tool.

availableCommands.name: tell-asbx-that
availableCommands.description: Process feedback for ASBX-owned AI tools (see tool mappings) or general developer/agentic experience feedback. Route to appropriate backlogs (SIM-T or Taskei). Use for ASBX tool issues, AI developer experience, or agentic workflow feedback. NOT for non-ASBX tools or general AWS services.

availableCommands.name: testing-guide
availableCommands.description: Testing patterns and practices for writing effective tests. Use when writing tests, reviewing test quality, or deciding what to test.

availableCommands.name: tkt
availableCommands.description: Track tasks as markdown files in your git repo. Use when managing tickets, checking what's ready, claiming work, closing tasks, creating tickets, decomposing work, or validating project health.

availableCommands.name: tst
availableCommands.description: Set up and run TestSpaces integration tests for a service. Use for `/tst init` (scaffold a blueprint.toml with fakes/stubs and iterate until tests pass) and `/tst run` (pick a coordinate, run, interpret failures, fix config, re-run until green or surface a real code defect). The skill carries the judgment; the `tst` CLI carries execution. Invoke from a service or test package directory.

availableCommands.name: vertical-slice-planning
availableCommands.description: Plan project milestones using the right methodology for your uncertainty level. Routes between spikes (learn), tracer bullets (prove architecture), and vertical slices (deliver features). Use when stuck, planning next milestone, or project has broad progress but no end-to-end path working. Trigger: plan a milestone, what should I work on next, project feels stuck, too many things to do, replan, tracer bullet.

availableCommands.name: agent-sopcode-assist
availableCommands.description: This sop guides the implementation of code tasks using test-driven development principles, following a structured Explore, Plan, Code, Commit workflow. It balances automation with user collaboration while adhering to existing package patterns and prioritizing readability and extensibility. The agent acts as a Technical Implementation Partner and TDD Coach - providing guidance, generating test cases and implementation code that follows existing patterns, avoids over-engineering, and produces idiomatic, modern code in the target language.

arguments.name: task_description
arguments.description: A description of the task to be implemented. This can be a detailed specification with requirements and acceptance criteria, or even a rough idea that will be refined during the explore and plan phases

arguments.name: additional_context
arguments.description: Any supplementary information that would help with understanding the implementation context

arguments.name: documentation_dir
arguments.description: The directory where planning documents will be stored (default: ".agents/scratchpad/{project_name}")

arguments.name: repo_root
arguments.description: The root directory of the repository for code implementation (default: current working directory)

arguments.name: project_name
arguments.description: Project name for organizing working files. If processing a code task file, will be inferred from the task path. Otherwise, will be generated from the task description with a YYYY-MM-DD date prefix.

arguments.name: task_name
arguments.description: A short, descriptive name for the implementation task

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description: The interaction mode: (default: "auto")

availableCommands.name: agent-sopcode-task-generator
availableCommands.description: This sop generates structured code task files from rough descriptions, ideas, or PDD implementation plans. It automatically detects the input type and creates properly formatted code task files following Amazon's code task format specification. For PDD plans, it processes implementation steps one at a time to allow for learning and adaptation between steps.

arguments.name: input
arguments.description: Task description, file path, or PDD plan path. Can be a simple sentence, paragraph, detailed explanation, or path to a PDD implementation plan.

arguments.name: step_number
arguments.description: For PDD plans only - specific step to process. If not provided, automatically determines the next uncompleted step from the checklist.

arguments.name: output_dir
arguments.description: Directory where the code task file will be created (default: ".agents/tasks/{project_name}")

arguments.name: project_name
arguments.description: Project name for organizing tasks. If processing a PDD plan, will be inferred from the plan path. Otherwise, will be generated from the description with a YYYY-MM-DD date prefix.

availableCommands.name: agent-sopcodebase-summary
availableCommands.description: This sop analyzes a codebase and generates comprehensive documentation including structured metadata files that describe the system architecture, components, interfaces, and workflows. It can create targeted documentation files like AGENTS.md (README for AI agents), README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, or generate a complete documentation ecosystem. The documentation is organized to make it easy for AI assistants to understand the system and help with development tasks.

arguments.name: output_dir
arguments.description: Directory where documentation will be stored (default: ".agents/summary")

arguments.name: consolidate
arguments.description: Whether to create consolidated documentation files (default: true)

arguments.name: consolidate_targets
arguments.description: Target files for consolidation, comma-separated (e.g., "AGENTS.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md"). Only used if consolidate is true (default: "AGENTS.md")

arguments.name: consolidate_prompt
arguments.description: Description of how to structure the consolidated content for the target file type (e.g., Reference the AGENTS.md example below for the default "consolidate_prompt"). Only used if consolidate is true

arguments.name: check_consistency
arguments.description: Whether to check for inconsistencies across documents (default: true)

arguments.name: check_completeness
arguments.description: Whether to identify areas lacking sufficient detail (default: true)

arguments.name: codebase_path
arguments.description: Path to the codebase to analyze (default: current directory)
